title: Resting rate-pressure product did not improve grip prediction in a prespecified cross-cycle spline test
abstract: An existing cardiac workload representation, pulse times systolic pressure, was tested for incremental combined handgrip prediction in separately sampled NHANES 2011–12 (n=4209) and 2013–14 (n=4635). Adding its spline beyond flexible standard demographic, body-size, pulse and blood-pressure predictors changed target weighted MSE from135.45019 to135.46439 kg2: reduction -0.01420, approximate95% joint PSU-bootstrap interval[-0.91818,+0.35827]. Source groupedCV also worsened; linear baseline, tensor baseline and reverse-transfer checks had favorable signs. This is a fixed-estimator negative point result, not equivalence, mechanistic evidence or proof of universal redundancy. Same-platform cross-cycle confirmation does not establish external clinical transfer. Author self-checks and clean offline reruns passed; no independent peer review claimed.
